coverage: Holiday-shortened session, Fri Nov 27, covering news since the Wed Nov 25 close
moodReason: Futures bounced sharply on Friday after a heavy AI and chip selloff, but markets still face a high probability of a Fed rate hike in December and firm inflation. Trading is thin because of the holiday, so the rebound may not hold.

stories.headline: Nvidia beats and guides above forecasts, but the stock still fell
stories.what: Nvidia reported Q3 fiscal 2027 revenue of $115.8 billion and guided to about $130 billion for next quarter, plus or minus 3%. Analysts had penciled in about $124.8 billion. The guidance assumes no data center compute revenue from China.
stories.why: Nvidia is the largest single driver of AI sentiment. A beat-and-raise that still fails to lift the shares suggests investors are worried about durability of AI spending and China exposure, which weighs on the broader tech complex.

stories.headline: Fed rate hike in December looks likely, with Waller calling for a half point
stories.what: Futures pricing put the odds of a December hike at roughly 73% to over 95%, depending on the source. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a half-point increase may be needed at the December meeting.
stories.why: Tighter policy raises borrowing costs and pressures high-multiple growth stocks. A larger-than-expected hike would tighten financial conditions further and could extend the equity selloff.

stories.headline: Inflation remains firm, with October consumer prices up 0.4%
stories.what: October consumer prices rose 0.4% from the prior month and were about 4% higher than a year earlier. Core prices rose about 2.8% over the year.
stories.why: Inflation running well above the Fed's target keeps the case for higher rates alive. That pressure on yields and rate expectations is the main macro headwind for equities.

stories.headline: AI and chip stocks drove a sharp intraday drop on Nov 25 before a late recovery
stories.what: The Dow rose 0.33% to 50,182.95 after erasing a loss of more than 1,100 points during the session. The S&P 500 fell 0.25% and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62%, after AI and chip stocks dragged the market as much as 3.2% lower in the morning.
stories.why: The intraday swing shows fragile sentiment in AI leadership. Buyers stepped in late in the day, but the pattern suggests positioning is still jittery heading into the year-end period.

stories.headline: Oil rises on Middle East supply concerns, with Brent near $98
stories.what: Brent crude rose to a two-week high near $98 a barrel after attacks on Middle Eastern energy infrastructure and tankers raised supply concerns. Oil was on track for its first weekly gain in four weeks.
stories.why: Higher crude feeds into fuel and transport costs and makes the inflation problem harder for the Fed. Energy producers benefit, while consumers and airlines face squeezed margins.

stories.headline: US futures rally Friday as global stocks rebound during the holiday
stories.what: Nasdaq futures rose about 2.1% and S&P 500 futures rose about 1.5% in early Friday trading. Asian and European markets rose while US cash markets were closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving.
stories.why: The rebound suggests buyers are willing to step in after a heavy selloff. Strategists remain split on whether the selling has run its course, so the bounce could fade quickly on thin volume.

watch.item: Early close at 1:00 p.m. ET with thin holiday volume
Regular trading resumes after the holiday; Nvidia guidance and AI stock reaction in focus
Fed decision on whether to raise rates at the December meeting

bottomLine: Stocks sold off hard before the Thanksgiving break and then rebounded in global trading, but the rebound is fragile. Nvidia's strong guidance has not yet restored confidence in AI leadership, and sticky inflation with oil near $98 keeps a December Fed hike on the table. Expect thin holiday trading to amplify moves, and watch the Fed meeting on Dec 9 as the main macro catalyst.
